$comment: Recorded exceptions to licence-policy.json. Consumed by scripts/check-licences.ts.
An empty exceptions list is the correct and desirable state. Every entry here is a
standing obligation somebody has to remember, which is why each one carries an expiry.
RULES, enforced by the gate and not negotiable in review:
1. Every entry needs spdx, package, surface, reason, compensatingControl, approver,
approved and reviewBy. A missing field fails the build.
2. An entry whose reviewBy date has passed FAILS THE BUILD. An exception that cannot
expire is a policy change pretending to be an exception.
3. Licences with exceptionsAllowed:false in licence-policy.json can NEVER be excepted
here. AGPL, GPL, SSPL, BUSL, Elastic, CC-BY-NC/ND and JSON are not available to
this file; the gate rejects such an entry even with an approver.
4. The approver must be a named human. 'QA & Security Engineer' is a valid approver
for a technical exception; anything with legal or commercial weight needs the CEO.
5. 'unknown licence' resolutions record the ACTUAL SPDX id found and the sourceUrl
where it was found, so the next reader does not repeat the research.

example.$comment: NOT ACTIVE. Shape reference only; the gate ignores this key. Delete nothing from it when copying - fill every field.
example.reason: Transitive dev-only dependency of the test runner. WTFPL is permissive in intent but legally sloppy (policy section 3.4).
example.compensatingControl: Dev-only, never bundled or shipped; upstream issue filed asking for an SPDX-valid licence; replacement tracked in AIS-nn.
example.note: Prefer replacing over renewing. A second renewal of the same exception is a signal to drop the dependency.
